role.altitude: The intelligence analyst keeps interviewing, planning interceptions with the legal team, decoding group language and judging what images and signals show; background searches, filling plan templates, first-pass translation and attaching images shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping case glossaries of code words current and checking machine translations
role.ambitious_version: An analyst who reads the gist of a foreign-language message the day it is intercepted and sends only the key ones to sworn translators.

tasks.short: Prepare the interview with background from registers, interview or interact with witnesses or suspects to collect human intelligence, write the interview report and record the intelligence with source codes.

steps.what: Intelligence analyst prepares the interview: questions and background on the person
Intelligence analyst interviews or interacts with witnesses or suspects to collect human intelligence
Intelligence analyst writes the interview report

loop.input: The audio of a recorded interview, transcribed on police servers.
loop.output: A time-coded transcript the analyst can search while writing.
loop.check: The analyst writes the report in their own words; any quote is checked against the audio at its time code.
loop.why_not_simpler: Finding a passage in hours of audio is slow.

steps.what: Intelligence analyst records the intelligence from the interview with source and reliability codes

tasks.design: Background on the person comes from one query across the registers the analyst may use. The interview stays fully human. Recorded interviews are transcribed on police servers so the analyst can find passages while writing, but the report is written by the analyst, because drafting tools have not been shown to save time on police reports.
tasks.previous_blocker: Background had to be searched register by register and recordings replayed to find passages.
tasks.enabler_now: Federated register queries and speech-to-text on police servers.
tasks.still_hard: Getting a reluctant witness to talk.
tasks.human_edge: Building rapport in a hostile interview.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation and replaying; the interview stays human.

reach.learn: Whether searchable transcripts help prepare follow-up interviews.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial, AI-drafted police reports were not written faster.
The police run their own language model on police servers.

assumptions: Boundary: one interview from preparation to recorded intelligence; follow-up is outside.
Input contract for s1: registers connected to the police query service.
Input contract for s3: interviews recorded where the law and the interviewee's status allow, about half of interviews; others are written from notes.

The interview and recording the intelligence with codes (a first record) keep their full time. s1 keeps 75 because one query replaces searching each register and writing the questions stays; s3 keeps 80 because passages are found in the transcript instead of by re-listening, for the half of interviews that are recorded.
unknowns: Share of interviews that are recorded.
research_questions: Are quotes in reports more accurate?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: checking quoted passages against the audio is part of writing the report and kept in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about a quarter of interviews may be recorded and fewer registers are connected (5.5); high: about half recorded as assumed (10.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify the targets, prepare plans to intercept communications in foreign languages or across borders, agree them with the case team and legal adviser, have them approved and sent for authorisation, and arrange technical set-up and interpreters.

steps.what: Intelligence analyst identifies the numbers, accounts and devices to intercept
Intelligence analyst prepares the plan to intercept communications: targets, grounds, duration, languages and interpreter needs
Intelligence analyst agrees the plan with the case team and legal adviser
Team leader approves the final interception plan
Intelligence analyst checks the final plan as approved: targets, grounds, duration and the prosecutor it goes to
Intelligence analyst sends the approved plan to the prosecutor for authorisation
Intelligence analyst fills in the technical set-up and interpreter request for the interception unit: by e-mail today, on a standard form after the change
Intelligence analyst checks the set-up request: targets, period, languages and interpreter hours against the authorised plan
Intelligence analyst submits the checked request to the interception unit

approvals.approved_version: The interception plan exactly as approved by the team leader in s4 and checked by the analyst in s4c, sent once to the prosecutor handling the case for authorisation; any change goes back for approval and a new check.
The set-up and interpreter request with targets, period and languages exactly as checked by the analyst in s6c, submitted once to the interception unit's queue; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: An interception plan template fills case number, targets already identified in the case file and earlier orders on them, so the analyst writes the grounds, duration and language needs. Technical set-up and interpreter capacity are requested on a standard form, which the analyst checks against the authorised plan before submitting it to the interception unit. The analyst also checks the approved plan and its recipient before sending it for authorisation. Choosing targets, agreeing the plan with the legal adviser, the team leader's approval and the prosecutor's authorisation stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each plan was written from an old example and requests went by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates linked to the case file and standard request forms.
tasks.still_hard: Grounds that meet the legal threshold.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which line will carry the conversations that matter.
tasks.altitude: Less form filling; legal and tactical judgement stays.

evidence.claim: Templates linked to case data fill standard fields of legal requests.
High-risk processing of police data needs a DPIA; data kept by purpose and term.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing the interception plan up to the authorisation request and set-up; running the interception is outside.
Input contract for s2: targets and earlier orders recorded in the case file by the case team and analyst.

Choosing targets, agreeing, both checks and both sends keep their full time; s2 keeps 70 because case number, targets and earlier orders fill in and the analyst writes the grounds; s6 keeps 80 because the form replaces e-mails and the request is still written. The team leader's time is outside the analyst's savings.
unknowns: Number of interception plans per year.
research_questions: Do plans need fewer revisions from the legal adviser?

incremental.description: Intelligence analyst keeps the template current with the legal adviser.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: targets and earlier orders are often missing from the case file, so little fills in (6.7); high: the case file is complete (12.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study communication code languages and slang, keep the case glossary, translate intelligence for triage, have sworn translators confirm what is used as evidence, and follow language training.

steps.what: Intelligence analyst studies communication code languages and slang used by the group and keeps a code word list
Intelligence analyst translates foreign-language intelligence for triage

loop.input: Intercepted messages in a foreign language and the case code word list, on police servers.
loop.output: A working translation per message with code words from the list marked.
loop.check: Translations are for triage only and are labelled so; anything used as evidence goes to a sworn translator; the analyst reads every translation of a message marked relevant, and translates by hand any message whose working translation is unclear or contains words not in the glossary.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sworn translators cannot translate every message quickly enough to find the relevant ones.

steps.what: Intelligence analyst has sworn translators confirm translations used as evidence
Intelligence analyst studies foreign languages in training

tasks.design: The case glossary of code words and slang is kept in a shared list in the analysis environment instead of personal notes. Intercepted foreign-language messages get a working translation on police servers, with code words from the glossary marked, so the analyst can triage quickly; every message used as evidence goes to a sworn translator. Studying the group's language stays with the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analysts could only triage languages they read, and waited for translators for the rest.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine translation that can run on police servers.
tasks.still_hard: New code words and mixed languages.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that an ordinary word has started to mean something else.

ambition.what: Triage every intercepted foreign-language message instead of a sample.

tasks.altitude: Faster triage; meaning and evidence stay with people.

reach.learn: Whether triage sends fewer irrelevant messages for translation.

evidence.claim: The police run their own language model on police servers, with retrieval over internal policy.
Automated decisions with adverse effect need human intervention under the police data act.

assumptions: Boundary: understanding and translating intelligence; the analysis of content is separate.

Input contract for s2: intercepted messages in the interception system and the case glossary kept by the analysts; languages the server model handles poorly (about a quarter) still go to translators first; s2 is priced at that share.
Sworn translation and training keep their full time.
research_questions: How often does triage miss a relevant message?

already_counted.description: Intelligence analyst reads working translations of messages marked relevant.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep beyond s1: adding new code words to the glossary is the list-keeping in s1.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the server model handles about half of the group's languages poorly, so more messages are translated by hand (16.5); high: about three quarters handled as assumed (23.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan what to collect, gather information with aerial photographs, radar or radio equipment, flag changes between images, evaluate the information and record findings with images.

steps.what: Intelligence analyst plans what to collect and with which equipment
Intelligence analyst gathers information using aerial photographs, radar or radio equipment
Intelligence analyst compares aerial photographs over time to find changes
Intelligence analyst evaluates what the images and signals show
Intelligence analyst attaches image crops and positions to the findings: cut and copied by hand today, attached by the viewing tool after the change
Intelligence analyst writes the findings in the intelligence file

tasks.design: Collecting with aerial photographs, radar or radio equipment stays with the analyst. For aerial photographs of the same area at different dates, fixed image differencing flags areas that changed, and the analyst looks at every flag. The viewing tool attaches the image crop and position to each finding, and the analyst writes the finding itself. No face or person recognition is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Images from different dates were compared side by side by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Image differencing on aligned aerial photographs.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a meaningful change from season and shadow.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a change on a farm or industrial site means.
tasks.altitude: Less comparing by eye; evaluation stays with the analyst.

reach.learn: Whether flagged changes lead to earlier searches.

evidence.claim: Aligned aerial photographs can be compared by fixed image differencing.
Real-time remote biometric identification in public needs prior authorisation; the design uses no recognition of persons.

assumptions: Boundary: collecting and evaluating images and signals; operations based on them are outside.
Input contract for s3: aerial photographs of the same area at different dates, aligned to the same map grid; radar and radio data are evaluated as today.

Planning, collecting, evaluating and writing findings (a first record) keep their full time. s3 keeps 65 because flags replace comparing every image by eye and the analyst still looks at every flag; attaching crops and positions keeps 15 for checking.
unknowns: Share of work on aerial images against radio and radar.
research_questions: How many flags turn out meaningful?

already_counted.description: Intelligence analyst dismisses flags caused by season, light or shadow.

incremental.description: Intelligence analyst sets the flag threshold per area type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few areas have aligned photo series, so most images are still compared by eye (6.8); high: aligned series for most areas (11.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
